incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: org=silverwood — sustained QPS spike (x12 baseline) + token errors rising. Impact: degraded tail latency and 429s for org-scoped routes. Pager: P1.
Marc (oncall): I’m awake, taking it. starting triage.
Alyssa (sre): I see their QPS hitting 8k concurrent requests to /v1/generate, mostly long-context calls. KV cache hit rate dropped.
runtime-team: Noted — most traffic is hitting the large-ctx model variant (redwood-xl). Fallback paths exist to redwood-large.
Marc (oncall): TL;DR mitigation plan: 1) apply temporary per-org rate cap increase for silverwood to avoid immediate 429 churn for important customers? (we usually *decrease* — this is odd). 2) throttle low-priority routes and disable async embeddings job that is spiking tokens. 3) route overflow to redwood-large.
Emma (support): Customer on the line — they’re seeing 50% failure on chat completions. We’ve promised a fix ASAP.
Lars (CS): I’ll notify their engineering lead and give an ETA once we patch.
Alyssa (sre): Confirming anomaly: their traffic includes lots of small-step replays from a training loop. We need to protect other tenants. Recommend: enforced per-org simultaneous-request cap (soft) and sync quick fallback model.
Marc (oncall): Executing immediate mitigations. First runbook step: set org throttle for silverwood to 250rps (from 100rps burst config) *and* enable feature flag to drop non-critical background embeddings.
Marc (oncall): Running admin API now:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-internal/v1/admin/orgs/silverwood/mitigate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"mitigations": [{"type":"temp_throttle","rps":250},{"type":"disable_feature","feature":"async_embeddings"}] }'
```
deploy-bot: deploy started: org-mitigation-config v2026.03.15-rc1 — rollout canary 10%.
Marc (oncall): Canary passed — applying to control-plane.
deploy-bot: rollout 10% -> 100% complete.
Alyssa (sre): Applying routing override to send silverwood overflow to redwood-large. Command:
```
adminctl route set --org=silverwood --primary=redwood-xl --overflow=redwood-large --overflow_threshold=200
```
runtime-team: Route applied on US-west and EU-west. KV cache warming in progress; expect tail latency to drop after a couple of minutes.
Emma (support): Customer reports immediate reduction in 429s to ~10%. They want to know what we changed.
Lars (CS): I told them we throttled non-critical jobs and shifted heavy model load to a slightly smaller model to stabilize. They asked if we can bump quota temporarily for higher-priority jobs.
Marc (oncall): We can temporarily increase the "priority_quota" for silverwood by 3x for 30m for authenticated priority keys only. Doing that now:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-internal/v1/admin/orgs/silverwood/quota \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"quota_changes": [{"key_type":"priority","multiplier":3,"expires_in":"30m"}] }'
```
deploy-bot: quota update applied.
Alyssa (sre): Observability: token error rate dropped 80%, p99 latency from 3.8s -> 1.4s for redirected traffic. System-wide noisy neighbor alarms cleared.
Marc (oncall): Good. Next: we need to plan revert and follow-up. Documenting runbook actions in incident ticket INC-2026-3487.
Alyssa (sre): Revert checklist: 1) remove priority quota bump (after 30m or earlier), 2) re-enable async_embeddings, 3) reset route overflow to default, 4) remove temp throttle.
Marc (oncall): Handing off to Alyssa for overnight watch. Key things for next on-call: watch silverwood QPS, watch p99 tokenize errors, and watch other orgs for spillover traffic.
Alyssa (sre): Ack — I have the commands and the incident ticket. I’ll keep monitoring for the next 2 hours and then hand to next rotation.
Emma (support): I posted a short note to the customer: "We applied temporary traffic shaping and routing to stabilize — you should see much better success rates. We’ll follow up with details"
Lars (CS): Customer appreciates the quick action and asked if we can avoid a full revert during their midday peak tomorrow. I told them we’d discuss after the postmortem.
Marc (oncall): Adding a quick note — we should consider an org-level ML-detection rule to flag training-loop patterns (high request rate + long context + repeated user-agent). Filing product request now.
Alyssa (sre): Incident moving to mitigation -> monitoring. I’ll update INC-2026-3487 with exact timings and config diffs.
incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager unassigned. :white_check_mark:
